newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-More shows in offshore well-Woodside.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-More shows in offshore well-Woodside.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday that the Keast-1 exploration well offshore Western Australia encountered hydrocarbon indications over a 65 metre interval, deeper than previously reported shows.
On December 31, Woodside said the well, in permit WA-6L, had appeared to intersect a gross hydrocarbon column of about 34 metres above a depth of 3,019 metres.
On Tuesday, Woodside, the operator, said the well was at a depth of 3,620 metres but operations had been suspended due to tropical cyclone Rachel now bearing down on the region.
"Hydrocarbon indications were encountered over a 65 metre interval, deeper and separate from the previously reported hydrocarbons," Woodside said.
"When operations resume wireline logging will be conducted," it added.
WA-6-L is on Australia's North West Shelf.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
